Also there is both @ExtendWith and import duplication.

Also duplicate import lines cause errors? Duplicate imports are allowed? Duplicate import statements for same class are allowed but may cause warnings not errors. In code they use @Test from JUnit Jupiter (import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test). The extra import org.junit.Test may cause ambiguous reference for @Test annotation? So need to remove the JUnit 4 import.

Also there is duplicate imports of org.ta4j.core.mocks.MockBarSeries and org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension, but duplicates fine.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments imported twice, fine.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.api.*; at bottom, which includes Test, BeforeAll, etc. Already imported earlier. Duplicate okay.

But ambiguous @Test will be problem. So remove import org.junit.Test; Also remove duplicate imports not needed.

Also there is @Test annotation used many times; we need to ensure using JUnit Jupiter's Test. So keep org.junit.jupiter.api.Test import.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.ValueSource; already imported earlier.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments; fine.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource; we need semicolon.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith; already imported earlier; duplicate okay.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest; duplicate okay.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.api.*; which includes Test, BeforeAll, AfterAll, etc. That may cause duplicate but not error.

But ambiguous imports may still cause ambiguous reference if same simple name imported from two different packages. Here only duplicate of Test is from org.junit.jupiter.api.Test and org.junit.Test. So remove org.junit.Test import.

Also there is import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.ValueSource twice; fine.

Now check other compile errors: In method shouldWrapWithPreviousValueIndicatorEvenWhenBarCountIsZero, they call shifted.delegate() - need to see NumericIndicator class has method delegate()? Probably yes.
